title: Signal aging and archive policy notes
content:
Purpose

This is a working note to capture a pragmatic policy for aging telemetry signals (metrics + spans + derived panels) and how/when to archive, deprecate, or thin dashboards. Goal: reduce noise, control storage/cost, and keep operator UX high while preserving recoverability for investigations. This doc focuses on guidelines, mapping from probe->panel->alert, retention tiers, and an initial rollout plan.

Background/context

We have accumulated ~700 widgets and hundreds of metric series across inference pipelines. Many signals are low-value (rarely consulted) yet expensive to store/query (high-cardinality labels, long traces). There is no consistent lifecycle; teams add dashboards for one-off hunts and they stay forever. This causes: high query costs, long dashboard load times, and cognitive overload for oncall.

High-level principles

- Signals are owned. Every metric/span/widget must be mapped to an owner (person or team) and a minimum SLO or use-case.
- Tiered retention: not all telemetry needs indefinite retention — apply retention based on business value and usage.
- Recoverability: archival should preserve raw payload for at least one forensic window (30 days default) before irreversible deletion.
- Low friction: policy must be lightweight to adopt; we prefer automation + slack reminders instead of heavy approvals.

Signal taxonomy and suggested tiers

1) Tier A (Investigate & SLA-critical) — 12 months hot retention
- SLI metrics (e.g., request_p95_latency, error_rate by tenant)
- Full trace spans for sampled requests tied to incidents
- Dashboards used in runbooks and playbooks
When to use: required for SLO reporting and regulatory/customer audits.

2) Tier B (Operational + debugging) — 90 days hot, 365 days archived
- Internal service metrics (kvcache_warmth_by_model, batch_efficiency)
- Medium-cardinality traces with session context
- Dashboards used weekly/biweekly for ops/engineering

3) Tier C (Investigative / experiment) — 30 days hot, 365 days archived (low-resolution)
- Experiment metrics, one-off probes, high-cardinality diagnostic labels
- Traces sampled aggressively then downsampled for archive
- Dashboards tagged experimental or ad-hoc

4) Tier D (Ephemeral / telemetry scratchpad) — 14 days then archive/auto-delete
- Notebook probes and ad-hoc dashboards created during an incident or R&D spike
- No alerts; must be explicitly promoted to Tier C/B/A by owner

Metric and trace handling rules

- Metric definitions: canonical metric name, owner, SLI? (Y/N), cardinality notes, typical retention tier. Add to instrumentation registry (link above).
- Labels: high-cardinality labels must have explicit guardrails. Default policy: any label with >1000 unique values in 7 days must be flagged and moved to label_bag or dropped at ingestion unless owner requests exemption.
- Traces: implement severity-weighted sampling for traces: always sample traces that correlate to errors or high-latency (> p99 threshold). For low-priority endpoints, use reservoir sampling to cap traces per minute. Archive strategy: store full traces 30d, then store head-metadata (span IDs, minimal annotations) for 1yr.

Dashboard lifecycle and migration notes

- Dashboard metadata required: owner, team, primary use-case, retention_tier, last_reviewed date. Add to dashboard registry and surface in the Console.
- Migration path for old dashboards:
  1) Auto-scan dashboards with no views in 90 days -> notify owner with suggested action (delete, archive, promote).
  2) If no response in 30 days -> move to "archived dashboards" folder (read-only) and set retention_tier=Tier C/D.
  3) After archived retention window -> delete or persist as JSON export for audits.
- Practical heuristics for dashboard pruning:
  - If >60% panels rely on experimental metrics (Tier C/D), mark dashboard as experimental.
  - Dashboards with >10 high-cardinality panels should be split by tenant or summarized with rollups.

Tracing-specific recommendations

- Trace context propagation: ensure token/request id flows from API -> router -> runtime -> cache -> model server. Add an observed span tag "kvcache_warmth_bucket" to help attribute latency.
- Sampling budget: define per-cluster budgets (traces/min) prioritized by tier and by incident flag. On incidents, temporarily raise sampling for affected tenant.
- Trace retention/obfuscation: traces containing PII or prompt content must be redacted at ingestion or routed to a private vault per Private deployment rules. Add a PII detection hook.

Dashboards / Panel design guidance

- Prefer rollup and ratio metrics for multi-tenant views (e.g., errors_per_1000_requests) rather than raw counts for cost and clarity.
- Use heatmaps for latency slices by request_size and sequence_length distribution. Keep cardinality of heatmap buckets bounded.
- Limit per-dashboard query time budget in Console (default 5s). Long-running panels >10s must be flagged and reworked.

Operational playbook integration

- Runbook link: dashboards used in runbooks must be included in a rollout-readiness checklist and be Tier A/B.
- Canary rollouts: probe metrics for canary must be Tier A and pre-configured to retain full traces for at least 7 days post-rollout.

Automation and tooling

- Build a lightweight dashboard registry and a periodic scanner (Lambda/cron) that: collects last_viewed, query_cost_estimate, cardinality flags, and notifies owners. Refer to ENGOBS-3421 for the scanner backlog.
- Add an ingestion hook to rewrite or coerce labels flagged as high-cardinality to a label_bag (free-text) plus a low-cardinality summary label.
- Provide a one-click "promote to Tier B" flow in Console for owners to lengthen retention for signals they care about.

Rollout plan (Q4 initial runway)

- Week 0-2: finalize tiers and acceptance criteria (this doc). Create dashboard/metric registry schema (owner, use-case, tier).
- Week 3-6: implement scanner + slack notifier (ENGOBS-3421). Start small: teams serving runtime + observability.
- Week 7-10: add ingestion hooks for label guardrail and a trace sampling controller.
- Week 11-14: auto-archive workflow in Console, dashboard folder for archived items, and export flow for audits.
- Post rollout: monthly reviews and a metrics debt sprint every quarter.

Open questions / unresolved items

- What is the maximum archive retrieval latency we are comfortable with for forensic queries? 24h? 72h? (OPS input needed)
- Should we chargeback query-cost for archived retrievals to the team that owns the signal? (Finance & product input)
- How to handle dashboards shared cross-team with no clear owner? Proposal: tag "orphan" -> route to platform-observability triage pool.

Action items (owners + ETA)

- Create initial dashboard registry schema (Priya) — ETA 2024-10-04
- Prototype scanner that emits unused-dashboard alerts (Ethan) — ETA 2024-10-25
- Add label guardrail to ingestion (Marta) — ETA 2024-11-08
- Draft runbook update to require dashboard metadata before new alerts (Jia) — ETA 2024-11-01

Notes to self / collaboration hints

- Keep policy lightweight: if the review friction is >2 touches, teams will bypass it. Prefer automated nudges + simple promote button.
- We should surface a small "telemetry cost" estimate per metric and per dashboard in Console — this will help drive right-sizing.
- Link to existing instrumentation registry: https://confluence.redwood/instrumentation/signal-lifecycle

If you're reading this and maintain a dashboard: add your name and set a tier. I'll run the scanner in 2 weeks and ping everyone with candidates for archive.
